description: Phase-WIKI-B Wave A — retrieval engine + orphan-vector cleanup. 4 stories that compose vertically to replace today's 7-call/30s wiki navigation pattern with 1-call/<5s. Plan: docs/wiki-retrieval-research/phase-wiki-b-plan-2026-05-21.md. Research: docs/wiki-retrieval-research/{graphify-full-pipeline,state-of-art,aura-gaps-and-phase-wiki-b-sketch,markitdown-best-use}-2026-05-21.md. Pre-shipped Wave 0 (commit 570696b3): wiki_page cross-tool read hint + accurate fusion package comment. STRATEGIC PRIORITY: per user decision 2026-05-21 the wiki bedrock blocks every other staged phase (Phase-ONB / Phase-RAG / Phase-KV / Phase-MCP-UI / MCP roundup) — none ships until Wave A+B+C test matrix is green across all complex file types. Wave A focuses on the RETRIEVAL ENGINE (B02 hybrid fusion + B04 heading subnodes + B01 wiki_subgraph tool with PPR seeding) PLUS B11 orphan-vector cleanup (discovered 2026-05-21 — Qdrant retains records for wiki pages deleted from disk; live observed as prova-wiki-20260518-204531 still ranking score 0.54 even though the file was removed days ago). Wave B (ingest robustness with markitdown plugins) and Wave C (entity dedup + reranking + lazy summarization) follow. STRICT one-story-exit per scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Wire hybrid FTS5+vector+exact fusion on the wiki search path
userStories.description: Today qdrantRepository.Search in internal/storage/search/qdrant.go ships vector-only for the wiki search path; only compact-memory drives the existing reciprocal-rank-fusion helper mergeHybridResults in internal/storage/search/search.go. As a result, search_memory for the wiki returns embedding-only nearest-neighbors — observed live 2026-05-21: query 'Delta Automazioni' returned 10 hits including a 2-day-old test page prova-wiki-20260518-204531 scoring 0.54 because cosine alone has no lexical anchor. This story wires the SAME mergeHybridResults RRF that compact-memory already uses through to the wiki path so the noisy result is downranked by the missing literal token. (a) ARCHITECTURE: identify the wiki callsite into qdrantRepository.Search (likely Search/SearchHybrid/related methods in qdrant.go around line 96). Add a sibling exact-match SQL query (LIKE-based or FTS5 phrase) against the wiki SQLite mirror + the existing FTS5 BM25 query. Wrap all three signals (ScoreExact, ScoreFTS, ScoreVector) into a single response set fed through mergeHybridResults. (b) BACKWARD COMPAT: keep the vector-only Search method intact and add a SearchHybrid method (or extend Search with a hybrid: bool option, default false) so compact-memory's own RRF call path is untouched. The wiki tool (search_memory) is the consumer that flips to hybrid. (c) SCORING: ScoreExact = 1.0 if substring of any tokenized query term appears in the page title or top-level heading (case-insensitive after diacritic strip); ScoreFTS = BM25 from FTS5 mirror; ScoreVector = cosine from Qdrant. RRF k=60 standard (mergeHybridResults already uses this). (d) DIACRITIC NORMALIZATION at query AND index time so 'Delta Automazioni' matches 'DELTA AUTOMAZIONI SRL' — apply the existing strip-diacritics function used elsewhere; if absent, add a tiny one in stringx. (e) BENCHMARK + ASSERT: extend internal/storage/search/search_test.go (or add new wiki_hybrid_test.go) with a table-driven case: ingest 5 mock wiki pages including a noise page that ranks high on vector but lacks the query term, query for that term, assert the noise page drops below the legitimate page. (f) NO new Qdrant collection. NO new SQLite table — reuse the existing wiki FTS5 mirror.

userStories.title: Heading-level subnodes — H2/H3 become sub-nodes with parent_slug + heading_path
userStories.description: Today Aura's wiki graph nodes are PAGE-level. A page like wiki/source-ruocci-email.md with an `## Extracted Entities` section listing many sub-items (one per customer) appears as a SINGLE node in GraphIndex. When search hits that page, BFS/Neighbors expansion explores neighbors of the whole page — not the specific subsection. Result: token budget wasted re-loading the entire page. Graphify's extract.py:4837-4944 decomposes markdown into per-heading sub-nodes (regex-only, no tree-sitter) with parent_slug + heading_path metadata. For Aura today this means: each ## section (and optionally ### subsection) becomes a sub-node addressable as `<page-slug>#<heading-anchor>`. BFS over the subnode graph returns the SECTION that actually mentions the query term, not the whole page. (a) PARSE: extend internal/wiki/parser.go (or whichever file reads page bodies — grep) to extract heading hierarchy AFTER frontmatter parsing. Use a tiny regex: `^(#{2,3})\s+(.+)$` for H2 and H3 only. H1 is the page title (already in frontmatter). H4+ ignored in v0. (b) NODE MODEL: extend internal/wiki/graph_index.go NodeMeta with optional Subnodes []SubnodeMeta where each Subnode has {AnchorSlug string (lowercased + dash-normalized heading), HeadingLevel int (2 or 3), HeadingText string, ByteStart int, ByteEnd int}. The page's main NodeMeta retains its top-level slug. (c) GRAPH UPSERT: when LoadFromPages / upsertLocked runs, also upsert one node per subheading with id `<page-slug>#<anchor>`, parent_slug pointing at the page slug, no outbound related: edges of its own in v0 (parent edge inferred from id syntax). (d) BFS NEIGHBORS: GraphIndex.Neighbors(slug, depth) when called on a subnode id returns: (i) the parent page slug; (ii) any subnode siblings on the parent page; (iii) the parent page's outbound related: targets (so a subnode inherits its page's confidence-labeled edges). When called on a page slug it returns subnodes too (depth=1 includes them). (e) RENDERING: new internal/wiki/subgraph_render.go provides SubgraphSnippet(slug) returning the byte range from ByteStart..ByteEnd of the source file — used by B01 when emitting subgraph text to the LLM. (f) TESTS: internal/wiki/parser_test.go for the heading regex + edge cases (no headings, mixed H1/H2/H3, headings inside fenced code blocks must be IGNORED — that's the gotcha graphify documented). internal/wiki/graph_index_test.go for subnode upsert + BFS neighbors traversal. (g) NO change to wiki frontmatter schema. NO change to the on-disk markdown. Subnodes are computed at index time, derived from body content; pages stay editable as plain markdown.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read internal/wiki/parser.go IN FULL — frontmatter parser already extracts YAML; this story adds body-side heading extraction. (2) Read internal/wiki/graph_index.go especially upsertLocked + Neighbors. (3) Read internal/wiki/godnodes.go to see existing NodeMeta-style structs. (4) Read D:/tmp/graphify/graphify/extract.py:4837-4944 for the heading regex Agent A flagged — the gotcha is fenced-code-block skipping (otherwise ```bash # comment ``` becomes a false H1 match). REGEX DISCIPLINE: do NOT use a regex that crosses lines without anchors. Match `^(#{2,3})\s+(.+?)\s*$` line-by-line, with a state machine tracking 'inside ``` fence' so fenced code is ignored. ANCHOR SLUG: lowercase + replace whitespace with dash + strip non-alphanumeric chars except dash. Matches GitHub markdown anchor convention. ID COLLISIONS: two subnodes on the same page with same heading text get -2, -3 suffix. Document this. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: H4+ ignored. No H1 subnode (page title is already a node). No bidirectional subnode-to-subnode edges across pages (those are graph edges, not subnode hierarchy). Confidence labels on related: edges stay PAGE-level — subnodes inherit through Neighbors() traversal, not by copying. NO LLM call. NO ingest-prompt change — purely a parse-time/index-time derivation. INVARIANT: re-parsing the same on-disk page must produce byte-identical subnode IDs + offsets (deterministic). Use sort.Strings on the final subnode list before upsert. PERF: 60 pages × ~10 H2/H3 each = ~600 subnodes max. GraphIndex map operations O(1) — no perf concern.

userStories.title: wiki_subgraph(query, depth, budget) tool — PPR seeding + hub-aware BFS + token-budgeted render
userStories.description: Replace today's 7-call wiki navigation pattern with ONE tool call that returns a token-budgeted subgraph for the question. Combines the four primitives in the previous stories: (1) hybrid search from B02 picks initial candidates; (2) heading subnodes from B04 give fine-grained addressable units; (3) Personalized PageRank (PPR) over the wiki graph re-ranks candidates with entity-anchored relevance (HippoRAG 2 / LightRAG 2026 SOA pattern); (4) hub-aware BFS expands the top seeds with token-budget rendering. (a) PPR IMPLEMENTATION: new internal/wiki/ppr.go (~80 LOC). Function `PersonalizedPageRank(g *GraphIndex, seeds []string, alpha float64, iter int) map[string]float64`. Power iteration with restart probability alpha=0.15 (standard), 30 iter (converges fast on ~60 nodes), uses GraphIndex.OutNeighbors + Degree for the transition matrix. Cache the FULL-graph PageRank (no seeds = uniform restart) on first call; PPR with seeds = re-weighted restart vector. (b) HUB-AWARE BFS: extend GraphIndex.Neighbors to accept an optional skipDegree int. When degree(node) >= skipDegree, don't expand through it. Default 0 = no skip. Computed from p99 of degree distribution per graphify (~50 LOC change to existing Neighbors). (c) TOOL: new internal/agent/tools/registry/wiki_subgraph.go (~150 LOC) with WikiSubgraphTool implementing the standard Tool interface. Parameters: query (required), depth (default 2, max 3), budget_tokens (default 1500, max 4000). Execute: (i) call hybrid search from B02 with topK=10; (ii) take top-5 results as PPR seed set (with gap-ratio cutoff: stop including seeds when score < 0.2 * top_score, same as graphify); (iii) PersonalizedPageRank on the seeds; (iv) take top-5 PPR-ranked nodes (which may include subnodes from B04); (v) hub-aware BFS to depth from those 5 nodes; (vi) render the visited subgraph as text using SubgraphSnippet from B04 for each node + edge labels with confidence from US-WIKI-A03; (vii) truncate to budget_tokens with a clear truncation marker. (d) RENDERING FORMAT: each node line is `NODE <slug> [<title> | depth=N]\n<snippet>` where snippet is the section body from B04 SubgraphSnippet (max 200 chars per snippet); edges as `EDGE <from> --<confidence>--> <to>`. (e) PROBE: extend cmd/probe_chat with a `wiki-subgraph-delta-automazioni` case that calls wiki_subgraph("codice cliente delta automazioni", 2, 1500) against the existing ruocci-email-ingested fixture and asserts the response contains '615827' AND 'delta' AND elapsed < 1500ms. (f) Aura's main agent loop should learn to PREFER wiki_subgraph over search_memory+file/read for questions about wiki content — that's a follow-up prompt-engineering tweak, not in this story. The tool just needs to be registered + working.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: this is the keystone story. (1) Read the COMMITTED outputs of B02 + B04 — their code paths are dependencies. (2) Read internal/wiki/godnodes.go (TopByDegree) for the existing per-node walking pattern. (3) Read internal/wiki/graph_index.go Neighbors implementation for the BFS template. (4) Read docs/wiki-retrieval-research/state-of-art-2026-05-21.md for the HippoRAG 2 / LightRAG 2026 PPR sketch. (5) Look at the wiki_godnodes tool (registered in registry_scan_test.go) as the tool-registration template. PPR ALGORITHM: r_{t+1} = (1-alpha) * M * r_t + alpha * s, where M is column-normalized adjacency, s is the restart vector (uniform when no seeds, concentrated on seeds when given). Converges in ~30 iter for graphs <1000 nodes. Pure float64 arithmetic — no new dependency. SEED SELECTION: top-K from B02 hybrid score, K=5, with gap-ratio cutoff at 0.2 * top_score (graphify pattern). If only 1 seed survives the cutoff, that's fine — single-seed PPR still works. HUB AVOIDANCE: compute p99 of degree distribution as `degrees[int(len(degrees)*0.99)]`, floored at 50 (graphify default). Skip expansion THROUGH any node with degree >= this when not a seed. RENDERING DISCIPLINE: respect the budget_tokens cap. Use 3 chars/token approximation (graphify's heuristic, good enough for Italian + English). Render seeds first, then BFS order by depth then by PPR score. Cut at the last newline before the cap. TOOL VS API: this story ships the LLM tool. Whether to also expose it as an HTTP endpoint at /api/wiki/subgraph for the dashboard is a follow-up — defer. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO ingest changes. NO new RAG eval. NO query expansion (HyDE) — that's Phase-RAG. NO multi-turn agent re-querying — that's Phase-RAG. Just the single-call subgraph retrieval. INVARIANT: existing search_memory + file/read + read_source paths stay intact. wiki_subgraph is ADDITIVE — the model can still use the old tools if it wants. Only the system prompt nudge (in a follow-up commit) will make wiki_subgraph the preferred path.

userStories.title: Qdrant orphan-vector cleanup — purge wiki vectors for deleted-from-disk pages
userStories.description: Today there is NO mechanism that removes Qdrant vector records when their underlying wiki page is deleted on disk. The index reconciler walks pages-on-disk and upserts them but never deletes orphan rows. Result: search_memory returns hits for pages that no longer exist, with score 0.54 enough to outrank legitimate fresh ingests in the user's noise band. Live observed 2026-05-21: query 'Delta Automazioni' returned [wiki] [[prova-wiki-20260518-204531]] in top-10 even though the file was deleted from /workspace/wiki/ days earlier. Banked per CLAUDE.md rule 'BUGS ARE ALWAYS FIXED WHEN FOUND — NEVER DEFER' (added 2026-05-21). (a) RECONCILE LOGIC: extend the existing index reconciler (grep `reconcil` in internal/storage/search/ and internal/agent/tools/index/ — there's a tool reconciler at internal/agent/tools/index/reconciler.go that's a good architectural template). New function `ReconcileWikiQdrantWithDisk(ctx, qdrant, fts5DB, wikiDir, logger) (deletedSlugs []string, err error)`: (i) list all distinct slugs in the Qdrant wiki collection; (ii) list all *.md files in wikiDir; (iii) compute orphan set = qdrant-slugs ∖ disk-slugs; (iv) issue Qdrant delete-points for the orphan slugs (batch ≤256); (v) issue FTS5 delete-rows for the same slugs (the SQLite mirror is the parallel store); (vi) log each delete with reason='orphan'. (b) TRIGGERS: run reconcile at (i) Aura boot, (ii) fsnotify event on wikiDir = file deletion, (iii) periodic ticker every 1h. Same trigger pattern as the existing tool reconciler. (c) SAFETY: hard floor — if the orphan set is > 50% of total wiki slugs, REFUSE the reconcile and log an error (likely a filesystem mount issue, not real deletions). (d) METRICS: emit slog at INFO when N>0 vectors are pruned (with slugs at DEBUG level only). (e) PROBE: extend cmd/probe_chat or add a small cmd/debug_reconcile that (i) creates a fake-orphan test slug in Qdrant + FTS5, (ii) runs ReconcileWikiQdrantWithDisk, (iii) asserts the test slug is gone from both stores. (f) BACKWARDS COMPAT: on first run after this story ships, the wiki Qdrant collection will likely have many orphans from a year of accumulation. The hard-floor in (c) protects against false-positive mass deletion (if the wikiDir is mis-mounted, refuse instead of nuke).

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read internal/agent/tools/index/reconciler.go IN FULL — it's the architectural template (boot + fsnotify + periodic triggers). (2) Read internal/storage/search/qdrant.go to find: how to list-all-point-ids (likely Qdrant scroll API), how to delete-by-id batch. (3) Read internal/storage/search/sqlite.go to find the FTS5 mirror table schema + delete shape. (4) Grep `fsnotify` in internal/ to see if Aura already watches wikiDir for some other reason (probably yes via reindex on file change) — extend that path instead of adding a new watcher. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this story is the wiki Qdrant reconcile ONLY. Source-extraction collections + compact-memory collections + tool index are managed by their own reconcilers — do NOT touch them. INVARIANT: a wiki page that exists on disk and was indexed must continue to exist in Qdrant after the reconcile — the diff is one-directional (qdrant∖disk = delete), never (disk∖qdrant = ignore). The upsert-missing logic is the existing reconciler's job, not this story's. PROBE FIXTURE: the easiest way to create a fake orphan is to (a) write a tiny .md file, (b) trigger the existing indexer to ingest it into Qdrant + FTS5, (c) `os.Remove` the .md file, (d) run the new reconcile, (e) assert both stores no longer have the slug. INCREMENTAL HARDENING: this story does NOT add reverse-direction reconcile (on-disk-but-not-in-Qdrant) — that's the existing reindex job's responsibility. Trust the existing one for the upsert side. ETHICS: log slugs only at DEBUG level. INFO log gets count + elapsed. Avoid leaking slug names that may contain customer data (per the standard tool-argument-privacy rule).
